conventions.convention: All derivatives are Cartesian derivatives in one fixed Newtonian inertial chart. Positive coordinate rescaling changes units and coordinates, not the observer.
Stress is tension-positive, traction is σn, (div σ)i = Σj ∂xj σij, and Dij = (∂xj ui + ∂xi uj)/2.
All five scales ρ₀, μ, U, L and c are strictly positive; ν = μ/ρ₀, Re = UL/ν, Ma = U/c, Θ = Ut/L and X = x/L.

The branches are separate: incompressible pressure is a constraint multiplier scaled by ρ₀U² after subtracting a constant reference pressure; barotropic pressure is P(ρ), scaled by ρ₀c² after subtracting P(ρ₀), with P′(ρ₀) = c² > 0.
Initial and boundary data are already-compatible inputs, with boundary traces and outward normals used only where they exist. Their rescaling asserts neither compatibility nor solvability.
The periodic domain is the quotient torus; spatial derivatives are derivatives of periodic lifts. The numerical parameters are exact illustrative inputs, not measurements.

load_bearing.statement: Under the explicitly stated smooth, unforced model branches and positive scales, the incompressible equations transform exactly to ∂Θu* + (u*·∇X)u* = −∇Xp*inc + Re⁻¹ΔXu*, divXu* = 0; the positive-density barotropic equations transform exactly to ∂Θρ* + divX(ρ*u*) = 0 and ∂Θu* + (u*·∇X)u* = −Ma⁻²(ρ*)⁻¹∇Xp*bar. Compatible data transform by the specified invertible maps, and total momentum on corresponding regions scales by ρ₀UL³ whenever the integrals exist. These are conditional coefficient identities, without existence, uniqueness, asymptotic or empirical conclusions.

The selected exact SI inputs give ν = 10⁻⁶ m² s⁻¹, Re = 10⁵, Ma = 10⁻² and Ma⁻² = 10⁴. On the dimensionless periodic torus, u* = (exp(−Θ/Re) sin X₂, 0, 0) and p*inc = 0 solve the scaled incompressible equations. In the separate barotropic branch, P(ρ) = 10⁵ Pa + c²(ρ − ρ₀), ρ* = 1, u* = 0 and p*bar = 0 give an exact equilibrium. The corresponding dimensional fields solve the selected models; no observation or approximation is asserted.
